Use the attached reference only for the costume, colours and body proportions of the character; drawing style, resolution and palette follow this description. Bottom row: 4 frames standing still facing right: 1 standing relaxed, mouth closed; 2 talking, mouth open, the free paw raised in a small gesture; 3 talking, mouth half open, paw lower; 4 standing relaxed, eyes closed (blink).

Isolated on a fully transparent background, no ground, no shadows, no glow, no frame borders, no grid lines. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Style: an expressive oil painting on canvas used as a background for a narrative role-playing game. Painted fast with very large flat brushes and a palette knife: few big strokes, thick impasto slabs with raised paint ridges and dragged, broken edges, every stroke left visible and unblended, bits of toned canvas showing between strokes. Shapes are simplified to large planes, fewer objects and almost no small detail: the rocks, the sea and the sky are a handful of broad, almost abstract slabs of paint; only the lit window, the lantern and the lighthouse get a little more care. No line art, no flowers, no fine rigging (each mast is a single stroke). Restrained palette of muted, broken colours: grey-green, ochre, dull violet, slate blue and earth brown, with only a few complementary accents of warm orange and pale yellow at the light sources. Not a postcard sunset: a cool, overcast dusk, the horizon band a narrow, dull orange. Mood: melancholic, quiet and literary, like a modern expressionist easel painting. Camera: a gently elevated view, as if from a first-floor window, looking slightly down onto the harbour; the quay runs horizontally across the lower third of the picture and its stone surface is wide and clearly readable, so that game characters can walk left and right on it. Composition for a game screen: the right quarter of the picture will later be covered by a dialogue panel, so place the lighthouse on its headland at roughly two thirds of the picture width, not at the edge, and keep the far right edge for sea, rocks and sky. Light effects and smoke are added later as separate animated layers: paint the lighthouse lamp only as a glowing spot of thick yellow paint with no light beam or rays, and above the chimney only a short, faint wisp of smoke.
